meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Unitary National Jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Civil Law framework of Napoleonic heritage with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation (Article 2, Constitution of 2014); commercial and corporate matters governed by the Civil Code (Law No. 131/1948) and Companies Law No. 159/1981
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United Kingdom BIT (1975, applied post-Brexit under UK continuity arrangements)
Egypt–China BIT (signed 1994, in force 1996, as amended)
Egypt–EU Association Agreement (2004) including investment liberalization provisions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing (as amended by Laws No. 181/2008, 36/2014, 199/2020) and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 401/2002 as amended); Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rulebook; Companies Law No. 159/1981 as amended by Law No. 192/2020 and Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95/2020) mandating UBO registers and disclosure to GAFI; Unit of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating (UMLTFC) directives and Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU) reporting standards.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — beneficial ownership declarations are filed with GAFI and the Commercial Registry; not publicly searchable but accessible to the EFIU/UMLTFC, law enforcement, and regulated financial institutions under lawful process.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and Egyptian domestic terrorism and sanctions lists maintained by the UMLTFC and Ministry of Foreign Affairs. PEP identification and enhanced due diligence (EDD) required per FATF Recommendation 12 and the CBE AML/CFT Rulebook; any PEP flag requires senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring. For this Low_Risk_Standard digital-health entity, simplified due diligence is permissible under Law No. 80/2002, but UBO identification, name screening, and sanctions screening remain non-waivable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Egypt Business Center (EBC) online name-reservation module (gafi.gov.eg / investinegypt.gov.eg), with cross-check against the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered corporate name must be rendered in Arabic script and must include the legal-form suffix for an LLC (شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة / LLC). A Latin-script English transliteration may be filed as a trade name, but it must be a phonetic equivalent of the Arabic name and must not create similarity with existing registrants. A purely foreign-language name is not registerable without an Arabic equivalent; transliteration should avoid diacritics and honor standard Arabic-English romanization to minimize registry conflict.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Securities, Exchange, Finance, Capital — require prior CBE/FRA special license and authorization
Ministry, Presidency, Government, State, National, Arab Republic of Egypt — imply government affiliation and are prohibited
Army, Police, Military, Defense, Intelligence — prohibited without ministerial security authorization
Islamic, Sharia, or religious references — require prior authorization from the competent religious authority
International, Global, World, Holding — require capitalization and business-justification documentation
Charity, Foundation, NGO — require prior registration with the Ministry of Social Solidarity
Health, Medical, Clinical, Hospital — trigger additional documentary review for digital-health claims; not licensable for the fitness-tracker scope unless medically certified
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, counsel shall file a written administrative reconsideration with the GAFI Company Registration Department within 15 business days, attaching up to three alternative names and a legal justification addressing the rejection grounds. If GAFI sustains the rejection, a formal appeal must be lodged with the GAFI Legal Affairs Directorate, followed by an appeal to the Cairo Administrative Court (State Council) within 30 days of notification of the final administrative decision. In parallel, a new name-reservation application may be re-filed immediately with alternative names at the applicable statutory fee to avoid delay. Extension of an expiring reservation is not automatic; the applicant must re-submit the reservation request and pay the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical Egyptian address evidenced by a notarized registered lease (Ijara Musajjala) or ownership title accompanied by a location sketch (croquis). A genuine shared-desk or flex-space business center lease may satisfy the requirement for this digital-health app, but a pure virtual mail-forwarding or post-office-box address is rejected. The Articles of Association must specify a real head-office address in Egypt.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical presence-verification visit during the first 12 months of operation (GAFI and Egyptian Tax Authority inspections under Tax Procedure Law No. 206/2020), declining to approximately 5–8% annually for a low-risk digital service company that maintains its registered office, keeps statutory books at the registered address, and meets filing deadlines.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; LLC formation and operation governed by the company formation chapters of the Companies Law and the GAFI one-stop-shop procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop for Company Establishment and the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Taasis wal-Nizam Al-Asasi) submitted through the GAFI One-Stop Shop for issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an LLC under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; stated capital is fixed at the founders' discretion in the Articles of Association. No escrow account is mandatory; if capital is paid in cash, a bank deposit certificate may be attached at filing to confirm the paid portion.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company as filed with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones. RESOLVED, that the issued share capital is subscribed and allotted to the founding partners at par as stated in the Articles. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at the address set forth in the Articles, and that the statutory registers be kept there. RESOLVED, that the founders named in the signature page are appointed as the first Managers, each with full authority to act for the Company. RESOLVED, that the Managers are authorized to complete Commercial Registry, tax, VAT, and social insurance registrations and to open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Portal (One-Stop Shop electronic window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an investor account on the GAFI portal, submit three proposed company names in order of preference, pay the name reservation fee online, and obtain the Name Approval Certificate. The certificate remains valid for 60 days and must be attached to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founding partners
GAFI investor registration form
Power of attorney if submission is made through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity or non-compliance with naming rules, resubmit alternative names within the 60-day validity window or file a written objection with GAFI requesting reconsideration of the screening decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Legalization of Founding Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Justice Notary Public and GAFI legalization desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bilingual Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic and English, have all founders sign the document in the presence of the Notary Public, and obtain notarial attestation of signatures. Attach certified Arabic translations of any foreign-issued identity and address documents.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Company Name Approval Certificate
Passports and national identity documents of founders and first managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the document for correction, amend the Articles and re-notarize the corrected version; no refiling with GAFI is required if the registration submission has not yet occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application through the OSS with the notarized Articles, name certificate, founders' identity documents, and proof of registered office. Pay the statutory registration fee and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and preliminary tax registration number from GAFI.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Company Name Approval Certificate
Office lease contract or usufruct title for the registered office
Passports and national IDs of founders
Bank deposit certificate if paid-up capital is actually deposited
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or deficiency notice, correct the documents and resubmit within 15 days; if the file is suspended, request OSS resubmission and, where the refusal is substantive, appeal the GAFI decision to the internal grievance committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Enrollment and Official Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office linked to GAFI OSS / Ministry of Trade and Industry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI OSS transmits the approved file to the Commercial Registry for enrollment; verify the Commercial Register extract and settle the applicable publication fee for the Official Gazette notice. The extract serves as the official evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by GAFI
GAFI OSS approval notice
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register extract contains mismatched corporate details, apply to the Commercial Registry for rectification attaching the Certificate of Incorporation and notarized Articles; the registry must issue a corrected extract upon confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, VAT, and E-Invoicing Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate registration through the ETA online services: obtain the tax card, register for employer tax and payroll withholding, apply for VAT registration if the digital app services are taxable, and activate the e-invoice/e-receipt system for issued documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registry extract
Registered office lease contract
Manager ID cards and signatory authorization resolution
Bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA queries missing documents or signatory validation, submit the executed board resolution confirming the authorized signatories and request reissuance of the tax card; late penalties are avoidable by filing the initial returns within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance Registration and Post-Formation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and GAFI post-incorporation services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NOSI, file the founders' and employees' enrollment lists, and obtain the social insurance registration number. This step is mandatory before the company can formally hire staff and is integrated with the GAFI post-formation clearing procedure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Tax card
List of managers and employees with national ID numbers
Manager appointment letters or employment contracts
Registered office lease contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI disputes contribution tiers or classification, submit payroll records and appointment letters for recalculation; any assessed difference may be paid in installments through NOSI's grievances process within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the LLC operates a digital health and fitness application under ISIC 6201 and does not establish an industrial facility subject to the Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial or manufacturing operating license is required for the fitness biometric tracking application and wellness telemetry services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 3 digital services with no physical discharge point, no wastewater generation, and no stationary emission source; an EIA report or environmental registration is not required for a pure software office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office-based software operations; any emergency diesel generator, if installed, must comply with Ministerial Decree No. 964 of 2015 exhaust limits, and hardware would be managed as electronic waste under Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire safety approval may be required for leased office premises depending on floor area, along with general workplace safety compliance under Labour Law No. 12 of 2003, including fire evacuation planning, electrical load inspection, and occupational health clearance for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; online services portal: https://tax.gov.eg and e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) complete Commercial Registry incorporation, (2) notarize and legalize constitutional documents and directorship authority, (3) register with ETA using the unified Taxpayer Registration form, (4) submit lease contract/usufruct or title deed for premise proof, (5) present official license/activity certificate where legally required, (6) obtain Tax Card (TIN and VAT combined) from the competent ETA office, (7) register for e-invoicing/e-receipts and obtain API sandbox credentials. Non-resident shareholders may act through a lawfully appointed Egyptian tax representative; all documents in Arabic must be attested.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available. Egypt does not recognize check-the-box or hybrid entity elections. LLC is treated as a separate taxable entity under unified corporate income tax law. A mandatory consolidated tax return can apply for subsidiaries under common control, but no entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for resident/established persons; non-residents supplying taxable goods or services in Egypt are subject to mandatory registration through a tax representative irrespective of turnover; voluntary registration possible at EGP 250,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory centralized e-invoicing clearances. Taxpayers must transmit machine-readable invoices (JSON/XML) to the ETA, cryptographically sign them and request an ETA-generated UUID acceptance before issuing to customer. Real-time validation via REST API/SDK; invoices must include QR code in offline scenarios. E-receipts (B2C) phase-in by turnover bracket is mandatory; non-compliance blocks issuance and subjects to penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of tangible goods exported outside Egypt and services performed and consumed entirely outside Egypt, including digital health app licensing/subscriptions delivered to non-resident users, are eligible for 0% VAT provided the supplier retains uncontroverted proof of export, receipt of foreign currency, and the economic ownership of the exported goods/service effective use lies abroad. The service supplier must permanently possess objective evidence that the customer is a non-resident and that no effective use or enjoyment of the service occurs in Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ACD / Cargo Tracking Number)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit/confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds in an Egyptian bank account
Service-specific export evidence: executed overseas consumption documentation, non-resident customer contract, IP/subscription user domicile proof, online telemetry export logs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA and Customs conduct document-intensive refund audits. Failure to prove zero-rating or late repatriation of export proceeds triggers: (1) retrospective clawback of VAT at 14%, (2) late payment penalties up to 15% per year, (3) fraud penalties ranging from 50% to 100% of VAT evaded, (4) administrative fines up to EGP 5,000,000 and imprisonment for felony-level tax evasion. Misdescribed of export documentation and artificial export transactions are treated as tax evasion and may expose the taxpayer and authorized officers to criminal liability and permanent loss of export incentive status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), established under the Central Bank, Banking Sector and Monetary System Law No. 88 of 2003, and exercising exclusive regulatory power over the Egyptian banking system, foreign-exchange licensing, monetary policy, and cross-border payment and clearing operations pursuant to Foreign Exchange Law No. 38 of 1977 and the Unified Banking Law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the 6 March 2024 currency reform, Egypt operates a market-driven flexible exchange-rate regime in which the EGP-USD reference price is determined by interbank supply and demand with CBE intervention limited to disorderly-market conditions. Current-account transactions, including software and application licensing, digital-health subscription revenue, technical services, royalties, and profit remittances, are freely convertible upon presentation of the underlying contract, commercial invoice, platform settlement statements, and tax documentation to an authorized dealer bank. Capital-account convertibility is restricted: inward foreign investment must be recorded under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and the CBE inbound-capital registration framework to activate the statutory repatriation guarantee; outward dividend and liquidation remittances require audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, proof of the original inward remittance, and the CBE registration validation number. Fitness-app revenue remitted from Apple App Store In-App Purchase and Google Play Billing is classified as service-export income and is convertible at the free interbank rate with no preferential spread.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All exporters of goods and services are required to repatriate proceeds through a CBE-licensed bank: goods within six months from the bill-of-lading date and services within three months from the invoice date. A mandatory currency-conversion tier applies to repatriated foreign currency; as a standing rule, 50% of export proceeds must be converted into EGP within 30 days of availability in the exporter's Egyptian bank account, with the ratio adjustable by CBE circular (historically raised to 100% during liquidity stress and relaxed after the March 2024 float). The undistributed remainder is held in an Export Proceeds Foreign-Currency Account and may be applied to permissible working-capital, import, and debt-service obligations, each supported by underlying invoices and CBE forms.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Egyptian law does not recognize foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) as corporate deposit custodians or clearing participants; only CBE-licensed banks may hold resident corporate deposits and execute EGP clearing. Foreign EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business, and Mercury are usable solely as offshore collection and invoicing conduits for outbound disbursements; every inbound capital item (equity subscription, shareholder loan, export proceeds) must ultimately be received in a licensed Egyptian bank account to satisfy the CBE repatriation, surrender, and AML obligations under Law No. 80 of 2002 and FinTech Law No. 194 of 2020. EGP balances held outside Egypt are prohibited, rendering any unlicensed EGP-clearing arrangement illegal.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one physical branch visit is mandatory for the locally resident authorized signatory, being the Egyptian-resident general manager or a director holding a valid Egyptian residence permit. Non-resident directors may complete remote video-KYC registration only if the bank receives: (a) notarized and apostilled constitutional documents; (b) certified parent-company board resolutions approving the account mandate and signatory list; (c) banker's reference letters from existing depository banks; (d) the CBE-mandated Ultimate Beneficial Owner declaration; and (e) an in-branch attestation by the local signatory before the compliance officer. Purely remote onboarding with zero physical presence and no local resident signatory is uniformly rejected by NBE, Banque Misr, and CIB.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident investor using a multi-layer offshore holding structure with nominee shareholding and no economic substance at the intermediate level.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership-chain diagram with exact percentages; certified registry extracts and certificates of incumbency for each entity; apostilled constitutional documents; executed UBO declaration per AML Law No. 80 of 2002; audited financial statements of the parent; banker's reference letter from the parent's depository bank; and a statutory declaration confirming the absence of nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volatility digital revenue profile with unverifiable mass-market end customers transacting through Apple App Store IAP and Google Play Billing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; monthly payout statements from Apple/Google treasury or the payment services provider; a transaction-level reconciliation ledger; the audited revenue-recognition policy; and platform country-availability controls demonstrating storefront-level geofiltering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk jurisdiction exposure in the fitness-app consumer base, particularly payment tokens originating from sanctioned or monitoring-list countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP-geolocation and storefront country-filtering policy; automated OFAC, EU, and UN consolidated-list screening of payment tokens, device IP addresses, and user accounts; PEP and negative-news search outputs; a written sanctions-compliance policy; and a legal representation letter confirming zero transactions with designated persons or embargoed jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder capital injection characterized as unexplained wealth or round-tripping, particularly when the shareholder is domiciled in a GCC jurisdiction without an evident nexus to the digital-health business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds dossier comprising salary records, personal or corporate bank statements, and investment or liquidation statements; executed share-subscription and capital-increase resolutions; GAFI foreign-investment registration approval where the FDI threshold applies; the CBE inbound-investment registration validation number; and a board-approved cash-flow forecast and business plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the shareholders' bank to the entity's USD account at the selected Egyptian bank, with the beneficiary stated exactly as registered in the Commercial Register and Tax Card, the remittance marked with CBE purpose code 1110 (Capital Subscription / Foreign Direct Investment), and the Commercial Register number and Tax Identification Number referenced in field 72 of the wire. The receiving bank must be provided, within five business days of credit, with the board/shareholder capital-subscription resolution, certified commercial-registry extract, tax card, and the CBE inbound-capital registration declaration. No statutory escrow or minimum capital is imposed for an LLC under the entity profile; GAFI registration is not mandatory for a fully export-oriented digital-services company but strengthens the outward-repatriation guarantee. Equity capital is not subject to the export-proceeds surrender ratio; the USD balance is retained in the capital account and converted to EGP for operational needs at the interbank rate under a CBE conversion form.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Digital-service disbursements, including Apple IAP and Google Play platform fees, cloud infrastructure subscriptions, software-licensing fees, and programmatic advertising costs, are settled by SWIFT MT103 with CBE purpose code for fees for technical services and software licenses; the bank must hold the executed service agreement, commercial invoice, the applicable withholding-tax certificate (10-20% depending on the treaty and service classification), and a CBE services-payment declaration. Commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700) are not appropriate for intangible digital flows and apply only to physical-goods imports, for which an MT700 sight LC with draft, bill of lading, and commercial invoice constitutes the required rail. Offshore PSP collections (Apple/Google payouts, Stripe, Adyen, PayU) must be credited into the Egyptian USD account with the remittance instruction reading Export Proceeds - Digital Services accompanied by the monthly platform settlement statement, which starts the three-month repatriation clock and activates the mandatory 50% EGP conversion requirement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based FX Forward Contracts with CBE-licensed banks, tenor up to 12 months, strictly backed by documented underlying service-export or license-fee flows; speculative forward-only positions are prohibited for Egyptian residents.
FX Swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) for treasury liquidity management around the monthly subscription-collection, tax, and payroll cycles.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on the EGP: accessible only to non-resident counterparties hedging an economic exposure to Egypt; the Egyptian LLC itself must hedge onshore and may not access the offshore NDF market.

Cross-Currency Swaps (USD-EGP and third-currency combinations) for structured foreign-currency funding and long-term balance-sheet hedging, subject to CBE prior approval where the notional amount exceeds the bank's large-exposure reporting threshold.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year company, generally by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines, tax-payment interest, tax assessment and collection measures may apply. Egypt has no universal automatic strike-off deadline linked solely to late tax filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and corporate records submission, where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and applicable commercial registry authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements should be prepared and approved annually; filing timing follows the applicable GAFI and company-law procedure, commonly after approval by the partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, filing rejection, regulatory notices and restrictions on subsequent corporate amendments may apply. Persistent non-compliance may support dissolution or administrative removal proceedings; no single universal strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partners' meeting and approval of accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; GAFI or other authority where filing or notification is prescribed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once in each financial year and generally within three months after the financial year-end under the applicable company-law procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager liability, potential penalties, challenges to resolutions and regulatory compliance notices may arise. No automatic strike-off is triggered solely by failure to hold one meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry and company information renewal or confirmation, if requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and applicable GAFI office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No universal annual renewal applies; updates are required when registered particulars change and periodic renewal may be required by the relevant registry certificate or local procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, inability to complete amendments and registry suspension or cancellation procedures may apply. The applicable authority determines any removal timeline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audit report, where the company falls within the statutory audit requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company, partners' meeting and relevant GAFI or tax filing records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before approval of annual financial statements and before any related statutory filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounts may not be validly approved or accepted for filing; manager and auditor liability, regulatory penalties and tax reassessment exposure may result.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC generally requires a statutory auditor where the applicable Companies Law thresholds are met, including the prescribed capital or partner-number thresholds, or where an auditor is required by the articles, partners or regulator. The current threshold must be confirmed against the latest Egyptian Companies Law and GAFI procedures before incorporation or filing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards, which are substantially aligned with IFRS, subject to Egyptian statutory modifications and applicable tax-book requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt requires identification and maintenance of beneficial-owner information under applicable anti-money-laundering and company-compliance rules. There is generally no standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for an ordinary LLC; the UBO record must be updated promptly after ownership, control or management changes. Share transfers require appropriate transfer documentation, amendment of corporate records and notification or registration with GAFI, the Commercial Registry or other authorities where applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers and authorized representatives

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 500-2,500 per year for a standard registered-office, corporate-secretarial and local compliance package; government charges and translations may be additional
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,000-5,000 per year for a small Egyptian LLC, depending on transaction volume, VAT activity, payroll, related-party transactions and accounting-system quality

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended by Law No. 176 of 2020)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic tax holiday for digital health app publishers. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits a 30%–50% deduction of taxable profit for qualifying fixed-asset investment outside free zones, and Law No. 152 of 2020 for small/medium enterprises may apply simplified tax accounting; relevant only if the Egyptian LLC owns servers, plant, or research facilities. Free-zone or SCAZ entities with an investment license may instead pay 1% of gross proceeds, but a pure app development business typically does not qualify without physical industrial establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Juridical Persons (ETA-styled 'Tax Return Model 4' under Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 72), filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) secure e-filing portal at https://www.etax.gov.eg. The form and schedule are labelled 'CIT Annual Return – Legal Persons'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the ETA also requires quarterly advance payments based on estimated profit with a final reconciliation filed in the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and final settlement are due within four months after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year LLC, the deadline is 30 April of the following year. A 60-day extension may be administratively granted by the ETA on request only for objective reasons.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Egyptian LLC, commercial registration number, investment file number, address of the head office, and certified place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation trading through a branch must state the Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) details, tax card number, and the name of the authorised Egyptian tax agent or legal representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, currency used in statutory accounts (must be EGP in Egypt), and any approved change of accounting period or previous tax year carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch must convert all foreign amounts to EGP at the central bank published official rate on the reporting date; no consolidation with head-office accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Egyptian-source gross income from the health fitness app: Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, subscriptions, in-app telemetry sales, advertising revenue, and software licences. Store commissions are included in gross revenue unless the seller is legally the store operator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the PE; revenue from non-Egyptian users should be excluded if no PE in Egypt and no Egyptian source rule applies. Attach platform reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct development salaries, cloud computing, server/telemetry hosting, payment processing fees, marketing, depreciation of app infrastructure, research costs, and third-party consultancy. All expenses must be supported by VAT invoices and certified bank payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing rules require that all charges from foreign parent or affiliates be arm's length; head-office general overhead is deductible only on a justified cost allocation, not on an arbitrary profit-shift basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowed expenses (entertainment over 30%, fines, statutory penalties, non-deductible donations), excess interest expense (thin capitalisation), transfer-pricing add-back, and prior-year losses utilisation not exceeding five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign interest, royalties, central management fees, and technical service payments are subject to source-country WHT before use; if the PE pays the parent, the expense is not deductible unless the transaction satisfies Article 30 of Law No. 91 of 2005.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income as gross revenue minus deductible costs plus tax adjustments, allocable state income (for residents) and set-off of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE taxable base is the attributable profit under the OECD authorised OECD approach, restricted to Egyptian-source business activities; capital gains on shares and immovable property are taxed per separate provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Tax, credits, prepayments and balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 22.5% headline rate, subtract quarterly advance payments, foreign tax credit where applicable, and arrive at final tax payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE is taxed at 22.5% on attributable profits; on after-tax profits remitted to head office, a branch profit remittance / DTA-limited withholding tax applies; attach tax residency certificate to claim treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 2% per month or part of a month of the outstanding tax, capped at 100% of the tax due, plus an administrative fixed fine of EGP 1,000–20,000. Late payment interest is also charged at 2% per month. A false return triggers tax evasion sanctions: imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and financial penalties of 100%–300% of evaded tax, with coercive seizure of assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends and in-kind distributions made by Egyptian LLCs to both resident and non-resident shareholders under Article 23 of Law No. 91 of 2005, unless reduced by an applicable Double Taxation Agreement. The 10% is final for individually resident shareholders and a credit or refund for resident corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the ETA: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty-state tax authority, (ii) a beneficial ownership statement and underlying ownership history (no contractual pass-through), and (iii) the DTA relief application/form submitted by the Egyptian payer before distribution, or within five years using a refund mechanism if the statutory 10% was withheld incorrectly. The ETA will match the TRC passport data and issue approval electronically before the payer may apply the reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 20% on payments for IP and software licences from Egypt to a non-resident; DTA treaty rates commonly 10%–15% (e.g., treaties with the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy). Interest: statutory WHT 20% on cross-border debt liabilities; DTA rates commonly 10%–15% for bank and trade interest, with domestic bank exemption after prior ETA administrative approval. App-store licensing royalties from a foreign publisher into Egypt are subject, in reverse, to the Egyptian payor's obligation to withhold on royalties paid abroad; all WHT obligations must be discharged even if treaty relief is pending.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian transfer-pricing documentation (Local File) is mandatory when the taxpayer's related-party transactions in a given tax year exceed EGP 10 million in aggregate. A Master File is additionally required where the same threshold is met and the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 1 billion. A Country-by-Country Report is required when the group's consolidated revenue reaches EGP 12 billion. All documentation must be contemporaneous and submitted with the annual return or upon ETA notice, in Arabic or English.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the UAE; however, Article 30 of Law No. 91 of 2005 enshrines substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, and general anti-abuse principles. An Egyptian LLC holding the health-fitness app IP but with no board meeting, no Egyptian employees, no server or activity coordination, and no commercial decision-making will be treated as a conduit for the foreign shareholder. The ETA may disregard the entity, deny treaty benefits, re-assign income to the true foreign owner, and impose branch-level WHT and penalties. For AML purposes, the LLC must file beneficial ownership data in the commercial registry; absence of economic substance is a red flag for both GAFI and the ETA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring Egypt-source revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, creating fictitious cloud-cost invoices, maintaining off-book digital wallets, or mislabelling telemetry data sales as royalties to avoid higher tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 133 of Law No. 91 of 2005, imprisonment for 3 to 5 years and a fine of 100% to 300% of the evaded tax; if the taxpayer is a legal person, the fine is doubled; assets may be seized by coercive administrative execution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the false return or direct the concealment are criminally co-liable; civil liability attaches to their personal property for the unpaid tax, delayed penalties, and restitution; courts may issue travel bans and impose custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a zero-asset Egyptian LLC solely to hold the health-fitness app IP, collect app-store royalties, and extract treaty-reduced dividends without Egyptian office, staff, server logs, or operational control; declared business activity inconsistent with actual conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the shell entity, re-characterise gross receipts as foreign profit, deny DTA benefit, impose 20% WHT on diverted royalties, and apply penal interest and 2% monthly additional tax on the under-assessment; Commercial Registry may be struck off under Companies Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The doctrine of beneficial owner is applied, and directors as de facto managers are personally accountable for refusing to file accurate disclosure; travel links to the shell entity trigger GAFI financial embargoes; repeated abuse leads to personal penal liability for the shadow principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the EGP 10 million related-party transaction threshold while failing to prepare Local File / Master File, not conducting comparability benchmarking, or signing a year-end payment to the foreign parent for app development services with a 50%+ margin unrelated to economic functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA adjustment of taxable income, 2% monthly interest until payment, administrative fine under Executive Regulation of Law 91/2005 for defective TP documentation, and potential re-qualification of payments as fees subject to 20% WHT; failure to file CbC report invokes additional EGP fines and enhanced audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to penalty as same-day managers if they intentionally certify an inaccurate TP policy; the ETA can pierce the corporate veil when proof shows that the LLC exists solely to avoid tax, making directors jointly and severally liable for the additional tax plus uncapped late-payment interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting ultimate beneficial owners from the commercial registry, failing to verify identity of large in-app subscriber merchants, operating the health-fitness app proceeds through personal account payment links, or in-bound foreign investment from sanctioned jurisdictions disguised as licensing income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 imposes imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines up to EGP 100,000; Beneficial Ownership Register violations carry corporate fines and cancellation of the commercial registration under GAIF directives; the ETA can additionally block the filing of a valid CIT return until AML compliance certificate is remediated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and the nominated beneficial owner may receive personal fines, travel bans and freezing orders; where the proceeds of suspect health-data transactions are found to be criminal gains, the court may order the seizing of the director's personal bank accounts and assets.
